evidenceAudit.scope: Adults with osteoarthritis: clinical diagnosis, therapeutic exercise and weight management, topical and oral NSAIDs, injections and referral. Verified against NICE NG226; doses and contraindications from FDA labels.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: Joint replacement referral thresholds not in NG226

pathophysiology.summary: Osteoarthritis is a joint disease of cartilage loss, bone remodelling and low-grade synovial inflammation, causing activity-related pain and stiffness, most often in knees, hips and hands.
keyMechanisms: Cartilage degradation and subchondral bone changes alter joint mechanics.
Weak muscles and excess weight increase joint loading — exercise and weight loss reduce pain (NICE).
Pain sensitisation contributes to chronic pain.

symptoms: Activity-related joint pain; morning stiffness 30 minutes or less.
physicalSigns: Crepitus, bony enlargement, reduced range of movement, effusion.
redFlags: Hot swollen joint — exclude septic arthritis or gout
Rapid deterioration, night pain, weight loss — atypical: investigate

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Morning stiffness over 30 min, synovitis, raised CRP.
Hip pain felt in the knee; spine.

ruleIn.modalityTarget: Age 45 or over with activity-related pain and morning stiffness 30 min or less (or none)
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Diagnose without imaging; image only if atypical (NICE).

clinicalManagement.title: Core treatment
actions: Information; therapeutic exercise tailored to the person (strengthening, aerobic) — pain may rise at first (NICE).
Weight loss if overweight: any loss helps; 10% better than 5% (NICE).
No acupuncture, glucosamine, strong opioids or intra-articular hyaluronan (NICE).

clinicalManagement.title: Medicines
actions: Offer a topical NSAID for knee OA; consider for other joints (NICE).
If topical unsuitable: oral NSAID at lowest dose for shortest time, with a PPI; consider GI, renal, liver and CV risk (NICE).
Do not routinely offer paracetamol or weak opioids (only infrequent short-term use when others unsuitable) (NICE).
Intra-articular corticosteroid for short-term relief (2–10 weeks) if other treatments unsuitable (NICE).

clinicalManagement.title: Referral
actions: Refer for joint replacement when symptoms substantially affect quality of life despite non-surgical care (see Hip and Knee Arthroplasty topic).

learningObjectives: Diagnose osteoarthritis clinically and manage it with exercise, weight and stepwise medicines.
